nodes.claim_scope: Naive straight-through 1-bit residual-channel bottlenecks, applied after attention and MLP residual additions in a small GPT-like character-level language model, underperform dense residuals at matched model shape over 200-step multi-seed local training.

reasons: local evidence artifact paths are present

followup.hypothesis: A 1-bit residual channel may become trainable if the sign bottleneck is introduced with a learned dense bypass or annealed gate, preserving early optimization while measuring whether the gate can decay toward a mostly 1-bit residual stream.
required_evidence: Same 3.2M-parameter Tiny Shakespeare setup with dense, naive 1-bit, and gated/annealed 1-bit variants across at least three seeds.
Validation-loss curves through at least 500 optimizer steps showing whether the gated variant reduces the naive 1-bit loss gap by at least 70%.
Gate or bypass diagnostics showing the model actually uses a mostly quantized residual stream rather than reverting to dense residuals.
followup.stop_condition: Stop if the gated/annealed variant remains more than 0.20 nats worse than dense by 500 steps, or if diagnostics show the bypass stays effectively dense.
followup.success_threshold: At 500 steps, the gated/annealed 1-bit variant must be within 0.10 nats of the dense baseline mean validation loss while retaining at least 75% of residual channels through the 1-bit path.
followup.title: Residual-preserving 1-bit bottleneck with dense bypass gate

nodes.title: Blinded Multi-Agent Evidence Ledger Counterexample Benchmark
nodes.useful_signal_summary: Tier 2 fixed-seed run covered 1200 tasks per method. Blinded evidence ledger reached 96.00% success versus 94.25% for the strong single-generalist baseline, 86.92% for unblinded multi-agent, and 80.67% for random search. nodes.claim_scope: On a synthetic anchor-ledger retrieval task with 8-32 training entries, a 0.66M-parameter pointer-copy transformer achieves reproducible exact retrieval in-range and at 2x train length, outperforming standard transformer baselines and a no-match pointer ablation.

reasons: local evidence artifact paths are present

followup.hypothesis: Training with a ledger-length curriculum or pointer-score normalization will preserve the pointer-copy mechanism while raising 4x length exact retrieval from about 44% to at least 90% without degrading in-range accuracy.
required_evidence: Three fixed seeds on the same anchor-ledger generator with train lengths up to 32 entries and evaluation at 64, 128, and 192 entries.
Comparisons against standard learned-position transformer, standard sinusoidal transformer, and no-match pointer ablation.
Exact retrieval accuracy, loss, parameter counts, runtime, and memory logs saved under results/ and logs/.
A stop/fail threshold if mean 128-entry accuracy remains below 90% or if the no-match ablation closes most of the gap.
followup.stop_condition: Stop if the curriculum or normalization variant is below 90% mean exact accuracy at 128 entries after the same 1200-step budget, or if gains are not specific to the query-key pointer path.
followup.success_threshold: Mean exact accuracy at 128 entries is at least 90% across 3 seeds, 32-entry in-range accuracy remains at least 99%, and the full pointer model beats the no-match ablation by at least 50 percentage points at 128 entries.
followup.title: Length-curriculum pointer-copy anchor-ledger retrieval at 4x extrapolation

nodes.scale_limits: Validation is synthetic, uses 0.6-0.7M-parameter models, trains for 1200 steps over generated ledgers, and does not test natural-language retrieval, pretrained LMs, or datacenter-scale training. The pointer-copy model drops to 43.9% mean exact accuracy at 4x length and 32.2% at 6x length.

nodes.claim_scope: On a bounded synthetic tiny-LM pretraining proxy, raw ensemble-variance data selection is harmful because it selects noisy examples; a simple mean-loss bandpass variant finds rare structured domains and improves rare-domain validation loss, but does not improve aggregate validation loss over random selection.

reasons: local evidence artifact paths are present

followup.hypothesis: On a small public real-text corpus, ensemble variance improves tiny-LM pretraining only when combined with explicit quality and coverage constraints that prevent noise and domain-collapse selection.
required_evidence: Real-text corpus with documented train/validation split and fixed token budget
Selectors: random, quality/loss-only, raw variance, coverage-constrained variance, and domain/diversity-balanced control
At least three seeds of identical tiny causal-LM training
Validation perplexity plus domain/source composition diagnostics
Ablation showing whether variance adds value beyond quality and coverage constraints
followup.stop_condition: Stop if constrained variance fails to beat random and quality/loss-only on aggregate validation perplexity, or if its gains come from domain/source collapse.
followup.success_threshold: Coverage-constrained variance beats random and quality/loss-only selectors by at least 2% validation perplexity at the same token budget, while no evaluated domain/source slice regresses by more than 1%.
followup.title: Coverage-Constrained Variance Selection on Real Tiny-LM Text

nodes.scale_limits: Synthetic token corpus; 2-layer tiny causal transformer; three seeds; short GB10 runs; no real text corpus, tokenizer, downstream tasks, GPT-2-small-class baseline, or large-scale pretraining.

nodes.title: Variance-Guided Data Selection for Tiny LM Pretraining
nodes.useful_signal_summary: Variance is a useful diagnostic for underrepresented structured data, but it must be constrained by quality and coverage. nodes.claim_scope: On GPT-2-small evaluated autoregressively on 64 Wikitext-2 test windows of 512 tokens, periodic attention-mass-weighted ordered KV pooling preserves next-token loss substantially better than same-budget recent-token truncation and uniform old-token pooling at budgets 32, 64, and 128, and is near full-cache loss at budget 256.

reasons: local evidence artifact paths are present

followup.hypothesis: Attention-mass-weighted periodic KV pooling will retain a lower next-token loss gap than recent truncation and uniform pooling on 1024-token GPT-2-small contexts across multiple text datasets, while an optimized implementation avoids the fp16 instability and most Python compression overhead seen in this run.
required_evidence: GPT-2-small 1024-token autoregressive NLL/PPL on at least Wikitext-2 and one additional corpus with fixed seeds
Same-budget full-cache, recent truncation, uniform pooling, and mass-aware pooling comparisons at budgets 64, 128, 256, and 512
Numerical-stability checks showing zero non-finite sequences in fp16 or a documented mixed-precision accumulation rule
A serving-proxy timing breakdown separating model forward time, attention-mass collection, and compression overhead
followup.stop_condition: Stop if mass-aware pooling fails to beat uniform pooling on either dataset at budget 128, produces any unexplained non-finite sequence after mixed-precision fixes, or requires attention collection overhead that dominates any practical cache-memory benefit.
followup.success_threshold: Mass-aware pooling reduces the recent-truncation loss gap by at least 50% at budgets 128 and 256 on both datasets, has no non-finite runs, and adds less than 20% compression overhead in the serving proxy.
followup.title: Robust 1024-token mass-aware KV pooling validation with optimized compression

nodes.scale_limits: Single model, single dataset, 512-token windows, one fixed seed, fp16 cache, eager attention with output_attentions enabled, and ordered contiguous pooled clusters rather than full arbitrary K-means; no optimized serving kernel, no larger model, no 1024-token context, and no multi-dataset robustness validation.

nodes.claim_scope: On sklearn digits softmax regression with 30% malicious volunteers, a commit-then-random-audit gradient lottery detects malicious submissions in proportion to audit rate and preserves accuracy only when audit cost is high under a strong -5x sign-flip attack.

reasons: local evidence artifact paths are present

followup.hypothesis: Combining random audit with norm clipping or robust aggregation can maintain test accuracy within 1 percentage point of the honest baseline at no more than 25% audit cost under 30% malicious -5x sign-flip gradients.
required_evidence: Repeat the digits softmax regression protocol with 10 seeds and the same 30% malicious -5x attack.
Compare plain lottery, norm clipping, coordinate median, trimmed mean, and full verification against the honest baseline.
Report accuracy, loss, audit cost, accepted malicious rate, and rejection rate with saved per-seed metrics.
followup.stop_condition: Stop as negative if all robust variants either fall below 0.956 mean accuracy or require more than 0.25 audit cost on the same task and attack.
followup.success_threshold: Mean test accuracy at least 0.956, within 1 percentage point of the 0.966 honest baseline from this run, with audit_cost_ratio no greater than 0.25 under the strong attack.
followup.title: Robust Aggregation for Low-Cost Verifiable Gradient Lottery

nodes.scale_limits: Tested only a CPU toy classification task, exact server recomputation, simple SHA-256 commitments, deterministic audit randomness, 10 seeds, 300 rounds, 32 selected workers per round, and simple sign-flip attacks; no home-network, privacy, incentive, Sybil, cryptographic proof, neural-network, LLM-scale, or multi-node evidence.
